name: Third Monolith
note: Unearthed in 2014 beside Hajjar al-Hibla. The excavation team used its dimensions to estimate about 1,650 tonnes. The stone remained at the quarry.
source_title: German Archaeological Institute · excavation report, fig. 6

name: Unfinished Obelisk
note: The ministry estimates 1,168 tonnes for the intended obelisk if finished. The unfinished block remains attached to the bedrock at Aswan.
source_title: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

name: Trilithon podium block
note: About 1,000 tonnes per stone in the German Archaeological Institute’s excavation report. The three limestone blocks were installed in the second course of the temple podium.
source_title: German Archaeological Institute · excavation report, p. 89

name: Seated colossus of Ramesses II
note: Egypt’s antiquities ministry reports about 1,000 tons for the original granite statue. The figure here is treated as an approximate metric estimate. The colossus was erected at the temple and now lies in fragments.
source_title: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

name: Lateran Obelisk
site: Piazza San Giovanni in Laterano, Rome
note: Rome’s official tourism office reports an original mass of about 455 tonnes. The obelisk was transported from Egypt and raised again in Rome in 1588 after it had broken into pieces.

name: Vatican Obelisk
note: A single granite shaft, brought from Egypt to Rome in antiquity. It was moved to the center of St. Peter’s Square in 1586.

name: Grand Menhir Brisé
note: Estimated mass of the whole stone when it was erected. It survives in four fragments. The rock type points to a source at least 10 km away.

name: Luxor Obelisk
note: The Musée national de la Marine estimates 220–230 tonnes. The western obelisk from Luxor Temple was shipped to France and raised in Paris in 1836.
source_title: Musée national de la Marine · The journey of the obelisk

name: Menga capstone 5
note: Researchers estimate about 150 tonnes for the fifth roof slab. Their study identifies a quarry roughly 850 m away and examines how the builders installed the slab.
source_title: Lozano Rodríguez et al. · Science Advances (2024)

name: Moai Paro
site: Ahu Te Pito Kura, Rapa Nui
note: Universidad de Chile estimates 82 tonnes. The statue was transported to the platform and erected. It now lies fallen. Other estimates differ.

name: Ishibutai’s largest capstone
note: The largest roof stone in the burial chamber is estimated at about 77 tonnes. It sits above the chamber as part of the stone roof.
source_title: Nara official tourism authority · Ishibutai Kofun

name: Stone 54
note: Approximate above-ground mass of the standing sarsen upright, calculated from its laser-scanned volume. Its buried portion is excluded.
